competitive_position_facts.fact: Agriculture and Turf operating margin rose to 16.6% from 10.3% even as segment net sales fell 5%, indicating cost and mix improvement during the down quarter.

Construction and Forestry net sales fell 28% and operating profit fell 46% in the quarter, a sharper decline than Agriculture and Turf, with management citing efforts to reduce dealer field-inventory levels in that division's outlook commentary.
Financial Services segment net income grew to $183 million from $175 million even as the two equipment segments' combined net sales declined.
Nine-month share repurchases fell to $263 million from $880 million a year earlier, while the per-share dividend was held at $0.76.

catalysts.description: Completion of the employee-separation programs in fiscal Q4 2020, targeted to deliver about $175 million in estimated annual savings [c4].
Full fiscal-year 2020 targets: net income of about $2.25 billion, Agriculture and Turf sales down about 10%, and Construction and Forestry sales down about 25% [c3].
catalysts.timing_window: remainder of fiscal year 2020 (fiscal year ends late October)

unresolved_questions: Whether the guided fiscal 2020 declines in Agriculture & Turf (about 10%) and Construction & Forestry (about 25%) mark a cyclical trough or a longer downturn.
Whether the roughly $175 million in annual savings from the employee-separation programs materializes once they complete in the fourth quarter.
Whether Financial Services' credit-loss provisioning, expected to weigh on full-year results, stabilizes or continues rising as equipment demand softens.

macro_context.item: Management cited the global pandemic and 'unsettled market conditions and related customer uncertainty' as expected to have a moderating effect on key markets in the near term [c7].
macro_context.business_connection: Directly frames the company's own cautious tone behind its fiscal 2020 sales and net-income guidance.

macro_context.item: Management's industry forecasts called for U.S./Canada large agricultural equipment sales down 5-10%, Europe down 5-10%, and South America down 10-15% [c6].
macro_context.business_connection: This is the demand backdrop behind the Agriculture and Turf segment's guided sales decline and its Q3 results.

macro_context.item: Management's industry forecasts called for North America construction equipment sales down about 20% and global forestry sales down 20-25% [c6].
macro_context.business_connection: This is the demand backdrop behind the Construction and Forestry segment's sharper Q3 sales and profit decline and its full-year guidance.

own: Agriculture and Turf operating margin expanded to 16.6% from 10.3% even as sales fell 5%, and Equipment Operations gross margin improved to about 25.8% from about 23.4%, evidence of cost and mix discipline during a down cycle, not just volume-driven weakness [c5][c10].

Nine-month free cash flow swung to roughly positive $3.5 billion from roughly negative $0.35 billion a year earlier, and the per-share dividend was held steady at $0.76 despite lower earnings [c8][c12].

The employee-separation programs are projected to remove about $175 million of annual costs once completed in the fourth quarter, a structural cost action layered on top of the margin improvement already shown in the quarter [c4].
flat: Management's own full-year guidance still points to declines in both major segments (Agriculture & Turf down about 10%, Construction & Forestry down about 25%) and full-year net income of about $2.25 billion, well below fiscal 2019's $3.253 billion, so the trend embedded in guidance remains negative even after this quarter's margin gains [c3].
The company explicitly attached 'many uncertainties' regarding pandemic effects to its own forecast, an unusually direct hedge on guidance that is otherwise fairly specific [c7].
short: Construction and Forestry sales fell 28% and operating profit fell 46% in the quarter, with management targeting a reduction in dealer field inventory -- a combination that could mean further production cuts before that segment stabilizes [c5].

Consolidated pretax income margin rose partly because the effective tax rate swung to 36.0% from 19.9%, so the net-income comparison also reflects a less favorable tax quarter, not only operating performance [c11].
Total borrowings rose to $43.1 billion as of Aug 2, 2020 from $30.2 billion of long-term debt alone at fiscal year-end 2019, a growing balance sheet during a period of declining segment sales [c9].

scene.voice: Farm and construction equipment maker reports 11% sales drop, guides both segments lower for the year, and announces layoffs with $175 million of charges.

claims.text: Q3 sales down 11%, full-year guidance down about 10% in agriculture and 25% in construction
separation programs with about $175 million of charges and $175 million of annual savings
agriculture margin expanded to 16.6% and nine-month free cash flow swung to about $3.5 billion

scene.question: Is a cyclical business cutting costs at the bottom, or a business in longer decline dressed up by margin discipline?

ask_friend.q: Is this a bad quarter or a bad cycle?
ask_friend.a: Sales fell 11% to $8.9 billion and net income to $811 million, and the full year is guided to about $2.25 billion with agriculture down about 10% and construction down about 25% [c2][c3]. Yet agriculture's operating margin rose to 16.6% from 10.3% on 5% lower sales, and equipment gross margin improved to about 25.8% [c5][c10]. Management's own industry forecasts have US and Canadian large-farm equipment down 5 to 10% and it cautions that unsettled market conditions and customer uncertainty are expected to moderate key markets in the near term [c6][c7].

Separation programmes completing in the fourth quarter carry about $175 million of pre-tax charges and are expected to save about $175 million a year [c4]. Nine-month operating cash flow was $4.1 billion against $0.4 billion a year earlier, and free cash flow about $3.5 billion, while the dividend was held at $0.76 a share [c8][c12]. Construction's operating profit fell 46% and the company is reducing dealer inventory, which can mean further production cuts [c5].

The last close is $199.50, a 12-month high, up 28% over twelve months against 16% for the market. Market capitalisation is about $63 billion, roughly 1.6 times last year's revenue of $39 billion (from the market snapshot and valuation panel in this packet). The company carries about $34 billion of net debt, most of it funding the captive financing arm that lends to farmers and dealers, so enterprise value overstates the industrial business [c9][c1]. The packet has no peer multiples.

claims.text: the company designs, manufactures and distributes agricultural, turf-care, and construction and forestry equipment worldwide, sold mainly through independent dealers, and also provides retail and wholesale financing for that equipment and other assets through its financial services segment; revenue is earned primarily from equipment sales, with additional revenue from financing income and services.

Third-quarter fiscal 2020 net sales and revenues fell 11% to $8.925 billion, with net income of $811 million ($2.57 per diluted share), down from $899 million ($2.81 per diluted share) a year earlier.

Management forecast full-year fiscal 2020 net income of about $2.25 billion, with worldwide Agriculture and Turf equipment sales expected down about 10% and Construction and Forestry sales expected down about 25% for the year.

The company announced broad employee-separation programs to be completed in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2020, carrying about $175 million of pretax charges and an estimated $175 million in annual cost savings.

By segment in the third quarter: Agriculture and Turf net sales fell 5% to $5.672 billion while operating profit rose to $942 million (16.6% margin) from $612 million (10.3% margin); Construction and Forestry net sales fell 28% to $2.187 billion while operating profit fell to $205 million (9.4% margin) from $378 million (12.5% margin); Financial Services net income rose to $183 million from $175 million.

Management's industry forecasts called for U.S./Canada large agricultural equipment sales down 5-10%, Europe down 5-10% and South America down 10-15%, alongside North America construction equipment sales down about 20% and global forestry sales down 20-25%.

Management said its top priority remained safeguarding employee health during the pandemic, crediting early safety measures with keeping factories and parts centers functioning, while cautioning that unsettled market conditions and customer uncertainty were expected to have a moderating effect on key markets in the near term.

In the first nine months of fiscal 2020, net cash from operating activities was $4.057 billion versus $404 million a year earlier, capital expenditures were $594 million versus $756 million, dividends paid were $718 million versus $703 million, the quarterly per-share dividend was held at $0.76, and share repurchases totaled $263 million versus $880 million a year earlier.

At August 2, 2020, total assets were $77.264 billion and total stockholders' equity was $12.891 billion (versus $73.011 billion and $11.417 billion at fiscal year-end 2019), with short-term borrowings of $9.075 billion, long-term borrowings of $34.037 billion, cash of $8.190 billion and marketable securities of $640 million.

Equipment Operations gross margin (net sales less cost of sales, divided by net sales) was approximately 25.8% in the third quarter of fiscal 2020, up from approximately 23.4% a year earlier, even as equipment sales volume fell.

Consolidated pretax income margin (total net sales and revenues minus total costs and expenses, divided by total net sales and revenues) rose to approximately 14.2% in the third quarter of fiscal 2020 from approximately 11.1% a year earlier.
Nine-month free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures) improved to approximately $3.463 billion in fiscal 2020 from approximately negative $352 million a year earlier.
